interventions.body: Postoperative prognosis depends on the preoperative PSA and the prostatectomy findings. Extraprostatic extension is documented. Positive surgical margins is documented. Seminal vesicle invasion is documented. Lymphovascular invasion is documented. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are needed to refine this prognosis; a future recurrence date cannot be established from surgical risk factors alone. The fixed estimated horizon is 27.99 months. This is a predicted recurrence horizon, not evidence of observed recurrence. The sensitivity range is 22.39–33.59 months; its coverage has not been validated.

attempts.text: The postoperative pathology reveals an aggressive disease profile, with the surgical pathology report documenting "Gleason 4+5 with tertiary pattern 3 (ISUP grade group 5), pathological stage pT3b. Extraprostatic extension was present; surgical margins were positive; the seminal vesicles were invaded; lymphovascular invasion was present; lymph node metastasis was present." This indicates significant local and regional disease burden. The biopsy findings showed a Gleason 4+3 diagnosis. Countervailing findings are not documented in the provided records. The presence of lymph node metastasis and positive margins are adverse prognostic factors. Missing postoperative PSA data prevents assessment of biochemical recurrence. Furthermore, the pNx status does not establish node-negative disease, and missing nodal sampling would widen uncertainty regarding the extent of disease. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are crucial information that would revise the prognosis.
